Iv'e played very few open world games, but even so, whenever I think of an open world game I really don't expect much but dying light is very different, the amount of new skills you unlock throughout your playthrough open the game up to so much more fun ways to kill zombies, and I absolutely love it, and the fact that this game's parkour mechanics are amazing, and if that isn't enough you can literally get a fucking grappling hook, which makes traversing the world so much more fun, and getting away from volatiles at night a much smoother time.

This will most likely remain one of the best open world games I have ever played hands down, I highly recommend getting dying light, on sale or not, it's worth it.

Other than a few small gripes, this game is awesome. Fun to play, engaging, lots of missions to get involved with... there's nothing to seriously complain about in the game.

That being said, I will mention my gripes. Sound attracts zombies to you. Even when you're not the source of the sound. That's annoying. Let something explode in the distance or some enemy start trying to shoot you, and YOU get attacked, even if you're nowhere near the source of the sound.

Zombies can and will appear out of thin air to cause 'tension'. This is a bad mechanic to use in most games like this, and will often have something you're ddoing interupted by a single zombi slappin you in the back of the head suddenly. I've also had exploding zombies appear and explode before I can react.

Other than these things though, which aren't SO bad, this game is great. I highly recommend it.

VAC is extremely unstable and downright broken on Dying Light.

Friend recieved a VAC ban for what can be explained as a glitch, turning in a Drop to a quarter master and his survivor rank was boosted to 25 giving him a legend.

While attempting to figure out what just happened he left to see if restarting would help and was VACed

Everybody in the lobby had VAC disabled aswell, so even more broken.

Not only is VAC broken, but there is 0 need for VAC to exist on a non competitive singleplayer orientated game.

Game itself is great, but sure does suck me and my 2 friends cant all play together now because of a system that isnt needed.

17 bucks wasted.

Great graphics and interesting gameplay, probably one of the better zombie games visual-wise. Parkour is great but some slight clipping bugs on rare occasions.

Not much else needs to be said, you kill zombies of different types without prejudice ala Left 4 Dead, fat obese zombies with explosive digestive systems, spitting zombies (presumably were french when they were alive), night prowling naked zombies and other colourful zombie characters.

Slaying zombies is timeless and therapeutic, it's like sipping a cup of tea and having crackers in the afternoon.

Storyline's interesting but expect the typical hollywood cliches(as with other games) when you have a protagonist with an American accent.

On a side note, the non-important NPCs all come from the same family. They all look alike and share the same wardrobe.

Dying Light is an amazing open-world zombie game. The parkour system feels smooth and satisfying, making exploration and combat very fun. Running across rooftops while avoiding infected never gets boring.

The day and night cycle is one of the best features. During the day the game feels normal, but at night it becomes truly terrifying. The stronger enemies, limited visibility, and constant tension create an incredible atmosphere.

The combat is brutal and rewarding, especially when using melee weapons and upgrading your skills. Crafting weapons and surviving in the city of Harran feels engaging.

The story may not be perfect, but it’s good enough to keep you interested, and the co-op mode makes the game better with friends. 

The DLCs The Following and Bozak Horde were really fun and added a lot to the game. The Following has a great map, the buggy is kinda cool and running over zombies was hilarious. Bozak Horde is challenging and fun to play, shame that it only had one location.
However, Hellraid was not good and felt boring when horde after horde of skeletons are attacking You over and over all the time.

Overall, Dying Light is a must-play for fans of survival, zombies, and action games. Highly recommended.

I generally liked Dying Light, but it didn't really hit me that hard. I enjoyed the story, there are lots of side missions that are fun to do. The characters exist, some moments are interesting, but I can't say the story was very memorable. I mostly just wanted to run around the city, do tasks and fight zombies rather than follow the plot. I liked the gameplay more. Parkour is really cool: you can run on rooftops, jump between buildings and quickly escape from enemies. Fights are fine, there are plenty of weapons, but sometimes it all gets a bit repetitive. Overall, Dying Light is a good game with a fun story. Playing was interesting, I just can't say it really hit me hard.

"Dying Light" (2015) is amazing game. It has everything a true zombies / RPG / FPS / Open World fan could ever wanted. It was worth the wait.

Amazing graphics, tons of interesting and addictive quests, huge open world to explore, big set of skills, hundred of weapons, crafting, creating, killing - if you like this stuff, you will love "Dying Light". And thats what you get in the day time, but when the sun comes down, at 20:58 - everything will change. Literally i have never had such an intense 15 minutes (thats how much time in-game night time lasts) in VG game before. You have to play it at least couple of times in the night - superb / scary and intense stuff. Creators have truly outdone themselves in this aspect.

As much as i love "Dead Island" series (except for awful "Escape from Dead island") - "Dead Island" is going to have one tough competitor from now on.

When „Dying Light“ was released I just thought „No, not another boring Dead Island zombie game“. But: I was wrong! Dying Light is a great open world game with a touch of „Mirrors Edge“ and a twist of horror. A little bit boring at the beginning, it opens it’s doors pretty soon and becomes one of the greatest action/parcour games I’ve played in a while. Graphics and sound are both great, story is ok, atmosphere is fantastic. Also you get a LOT of game here, sometimes repetetive, but at least 30-40 hours of fun. Sometimes I had to struggle because for me the „parcour“ part of the game played much better with the gamepad (360) while the „shooter“ part - obviously - played better with mouse and keyboard, but switching is no problem so who cares. All in all I really enjoyed my time in this game, thumbs up!

I remember playing this game 4 years ago at a friends house. I truly liked the gameplay and combat style.
Now 4 years later I decided to buy the game, after spending some time thinking which game to play next. I have to say; not disappointed. The game's graphics are still fabulous and the gameplay never gets old. Even though you sometimes have to do some repetitive tasks, you will never get bored by jumping over zombie's and slashing into them!

10/10 Would buy again!
